The location of the car seat installation is also vital for your baby's safety. However, if your vehicle doesn't allow for a secure middle seat installation, the rear passenger side is the next best option. Always ensure the car seat base is level and that there is minimal movement when tested at the belt path.

Elm Street Safety Center and other certified inspection stations offer free car seat checks by trained professionals. Perfect Natural Alignment
When properly set up, a hammock creates an ideal sleeping position for your body. Unlike flat mattresses, hammocks naturally contour to your body's shape, providing support exactly where you need it. The slight curve of a hammock helps align your spine while keeping your head slightly elevated – a position that many sleep experts recommend for optimal rest.

Research has shown that the gentle rocking motion of a hammock can help you fall asleep more quickly. Imagine the Earth is like a giant spinning top that's tilted to one side as it travels around the Sun. This tilt is really important - it's what gives us our seasons!

When the Earth goes around the Sun (which takes one year), different parts of our planet get more or less sunlight because of this tilt. It's kind of like holding a flashlight toward a ball that's tilted - one part gets more light while the other part gets less.

During summer, your part of the Earth is tilted toward the Sun. This means:

When the top half (Northern Hemisphere) of Earth is tilted toward the Sun, that part of Earth gets more direct sunlight and more hours of daylight. This makes it warmer, giving us summer! At the same time, the bottom half (Southern Hemisphere) is tilted away from the Sun, getting less direct sunlight and fewer daylight hours, making it winter there.

Then, as Earth continues its journey around the Sun, the tilt stays the same but now points in a different direction. Six months later, the bottom half is tilted toward the Sun (making it summer there), while the top half is tilted away (making it winter there).

Spring and fall happen in between, when Earth's tilt isn't pointing directly toward or away from the Sun. During these seasons, both halves of Earth get about the same amount of sunlight.

That's why when it's summer in the United States, it's winter in Australia, and vice versa!
